as_told.title: Blue Book special unit investigated 700 unexplained sightings

tellings.quote: From 1947 to 1969, a total of 12, 618 sightings were reported to Project BLUE BOOK. Of these 701 remain "Unidentified."

plain: The claim is that, while Project Blue Book (the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s) told the public that sightings were swamp gas or misidentified birds, more than 700 cases were real and unexplained and were handled separately. The lawyer Dan Sheehan tells Michels this on two occasions, passing on what he says a man told him. In one telling the man is Oscar Wolf, who Sheehan says 'worked directly with Project Blue Book.' In the other he names his source as Albert Stein, a US Army clerk typist assigned to Blue Book. Stein, Sheehan says, saw that 'while Blue Book had this whole buffaloing operation going on,' there were 'over 700 actual sightings.' Sheehan does not say which Blue Book record he means. The Air Force's own fact sheet on the project, from January 1985, states that from 1947 to 1969 'a total of 12,618 sightings were reported to Project BLUE BOOK. Of these 701 remain "Unidentified,"' close to Sheehan's figure. A special unit set up for those cases is Sheehan's account, which the fact sheet neither states nor excludes. If true, the public study was a front while the real cases were studied quietly.

discussion.text: The teller does not say which Blue Book record he means; the Air Force's fact sheet on the project says that from 1947 to 1969 "a total of 12, 618 sightings were reported to Project BLUE BOOK" and that "Of these 701 remain 'Unidentified.'", close to the teller's more than 700. A special unit for those cases is the teller's account, which the fact sheet neither states nor excludes.
